topics.title: Cellular respiration sequence
topics.description: Glycolysis, Krebs cycle, then electron transport

sections.title: How cells turn glucose into usable energy
sections.body: Cellular respiration converts glucose into usable energy. Glycolysis, the **Krebs cycle**, and the **electron transport chain** work in sequence so the cell can harvest ATP.
sections.sourceQuote: Cellular respiration converts glucose into usable energy.

sections.title: The three stages in order
sections.body:
1. First, **glycolysis** breaks glucose into pyruvate in the cytoplasm.
2. Then the Krebs cycle oxidizes pyruvate-derived acetyl-CoA in the mitochondrial matrix.
3. Finally, the electron transport chain uses the resulting NADH and FADH2 to make ATP.
sections.sourceQuote: First, glycolysis breaks glucose into pyruvate in the cytoplasm.

sections.title: Glycolysis is not the Krebs cycle
sections.body: Students often confuse the Krebs cycle with glycolysis. Glycolysis happens in the cytoplasm, while the Krebs cycle happens in the mitochondrial matrix.
sections.sourceQuote: Students often confuse the Krebs cycle with glycolysis.
